newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to import 1.83 mln t crude oil in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to import 1.83 mln t crude oil in 1997.

text.p: Sri Lankan state oil company Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) said on Wednesday it would import an estimated 1.83 million tonnes of crude oil this year, down from 2.05 million in 1996.

CPC Chairman Anil Obeyesekere told Reuters the decline was mainly due to a 45-day shut-down of the country's sole refinery at Sapugaskanda, just north of the capital Colombo, between the end of January and March this year.
But crude imports would bounce back again in 1998 to around 2.1 million tonnes, he said.
Obeyesekera said CPC's term-contracts -- principally with Iran, Saudi Arabia, Malaysia, Abu Dhabi and Egypt -- would be sufficient this year to cover all the Indian Ocean island's requirements.
There had been no spot purchases this year and were unlikely to be any for the rest of the year, he said.

"We normally buy as and when we require but this year that need will not arise because of the fact that the shutdown was there and we were able to manage our crude oil on the basis of our term contracts," Obeyesekere said in an interview.
"But certainly in the other years we have about 10-15 percent spot purchases."
